outputs: Synthetic text instances for training data augmentation

changes_made.explanation: This paper focuses on text classification model calibration, not NLG evaluation. The synthetic data generation is a means to an end (data augmentation) rather than the primary NLG task being evaluated. Therefore, all NLG-specific metadata was removed.
The paper uses accuracy and ECE to evaluate text classification models, not generated NLG outputs. These metrics measure classification performance and calibration, not NLG quality.
No LLMs are used as judges/evaluators in this paper. LLMs (specifically Llama-2) are used only for synthetic data generation.
No human evaluation of generated outputs is conducted in this paper.

overall_notes: This paper is fundamentally about text classification model calibration using synthetic data augmentation, not NLG evaluation. While it involves text generation (synthetic data creation), the generated text is not the primary output being evaluated - it's a tool to improve classifier performance. The core evaluation focuses on classification accuracy and calibration error of the downstream classifier, not the quality of the generated synthetic text itself.
